name: Refugee Recognition (UNHCR / Bureau des Réfugiés et Apatrides)

qualifying_event.description: UNHCR (not a dedicated national asylum authority) conducts refugee status determination in Morocco: registration (by phone/WhatsApp helpline, in-person at the Rabat office, or via partner NGO OMDH in Oujda/Tangier/Nador/Casablanca for those outside Rabat), a biometric registration interview, a detailed RSD interview, a first-instance decision, and a 30-day appeal window if rejected.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Registration request (identity documents not required to register); biometric data (fingerprints, iris scan) at the registration interview; detailed persecution account at the RSD interview.

requirements.blocker_text: Must meet the refugee definition per UNHCR's mandate assessment. First-instance decisions generally take about one month for straightforward cases but can take several months for complex ones; the registration-to-RSD-interview wait can range from several months to several years depending on case priority.

evidence_required.document: Registration form (name, nationality, family details, reasons for leaving)

outcome.duration_length: National Refugee (BRA) card: 1 year. Residency card issued by police after the BRA card: 1 year, renewable.

sources.title: UNHCR Morocco -- registration channels (helpline, Rabat office, OMDH partner offices), 6-stage process, ~1-month first-instance decisions (longer for complex cases), months-to-years registration-to-RSD wait, 30-day appeal window
UNHCR Morocco -- post-recognition process: 1-year National Refugee (BRA) card issued by the Moroccan government, followed by a 1-year renewable Residency Card from the local police department
GADEM legal guide -- explicitly notes Law 02-03 (Morocco's general immigration law) provides NO residence-permit category, short or long-term, specifically for asylum seekers

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Morocco). STATUS: DRAFT -- an important structural point: refugee status determination in Morocco is conducted by UNHCR itself (a UN agency), not a dedicated Moroccan government asylum authority, and per GADEM's legal guide, Morocco's general immigration statute (Law 02-03) contains NO formal residence-permit category for asylum SEEKERS during the (often months-to-years-long) determination process -- the National Refugee (BRA) card and subsequent police-issued residency card only materialize AFTER recognition, via administrative practice rather than a codified seekers' status. This is a materially different, more precarious structure than most other countries in this dataset, and is disclosed here rather than smoothed over. citizenship_after_months (60) uses ma_naturalisation.json's standard 5-year track since no refugee-specific reduced naturalisation track was found in the Code de la Nationalité Marocaine text reviewed (unlike Belarus's or Ecuador's reduced refugee tracks built earlier in this dataset).
